observations: Torah #119 is a mussar teaching about the universality of suffering in this world. The Rebbe observes that all people — rich and poor, great and small — are filled with suffering, worry, anger, and pain. He famously quips that while we believe the world to come exists, perhaps 'this world' also exists somewhere, since here it looks like Gehinnom. The practical teaching (eitza) is from the Midrash: since man is born to toil, the wise person redirects that toil to Torah study, thereby escaping worldly suffering and meriting the world to come. The entire teaching is structured as eitza (cause-and-effect advice), not bechina (shared-nature equivalences). The near-bechina statement 'this world is Gehinnom' is rhetorical rather than a formal conceptual mapping between distinct domains. Without 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain, no new packages can be proposed.
